content.text:
No, `user-service.js` still calls the database directly. It imports `query` and `update` from `../db.js` and uses the old callback style in all three functions: `listActiveUsers`, `findUser` and `softDeleteUser`. A comment at `src/services/user-service.js:3` says the switch to `UserRepository` is planned but hasn't happened yet.

`UserRepository` in `src/repositories/user-repository.js` already exists and has matching promise-based methods, so the migration would map like this:

| `user-service.js` | `UserRepository` |
|---|---|
| `listActiveUsers(callback)` | `findActive()` |
| `findUser(id, callback)` | `findById(id)` |
| `softDeleteUser(id, when, callback)` | `softDelete(id, when)` |

The project has a `migrate-module` skill that switches one service file from callbacks to its repository and then runs that file's tests. I can run it on `user-service.js` if you want.
